name: @pipeworx/mcp-federal-register

tools.name: search_documents
tools.description: Search the US Federal Register by topic / keyword for proposed rules, final rules, notices, and presidential documents. **Use this whenever the question mentions a SUBJECT** ("EV tax credits", "AI export controls", "PFAS regulations", "clean energy", "ozempic labeling", etc.) — recent_rules takes no topic filter and would return random unrelated rules. For a STRUCTURED count/list ("how many executive orders in 2026", "list 2026 proclamations"), pass type:"presidential_document" plus presidential_document_type rather than relying on free-text query — a free-text search for "executive order" also matches documents that merely MENTION one, over- or under-counting the real set. To find or confirm ONE specific executive order by its number, pass executive_order_number instead — it scopes and filters for you, no type/presidential_document_type needed. Returns title, abstract, agency, publication date, links, and for presidential documents also executive_order_number, signing_date, and citation. The response always echoes filters_applied: a genuine zero still says exactly what was searched, so it is never a bare empty result. Examples: search_documents({query: "EV tax credit", type: "rule"}), search_documents({type: "presidential_document", presidential_document_type: "executive_order", since: "2026-01-01"}), search_documents({executive_order_number: "14435"}), search_documents({query: "Strait of Hormuz", since: "365d"}). Pass `since` to constrain to recent documents — without it the relevance ranker can return decade-old docs for sparse-term queries.

query.description: Search keywords (e.g., "clean energy tax credit"). Optional if type/agency/since/presidential_document_type/executive_order_number already scope the search — forcing a free-text term onto a structured count/list question (e.g. "executive order") distorts it, since the term index matches MENTIONS of a thing as well as the thing itself.

type.description: Document type filter: "rule", "proposed_rule", "notice", "presidential_document" — mapped internally to the Federal Register API's own codes (RULE/PRORULE/NOTICE/PRESDOCU); an unrecognized value is refused rather than silently matching nothing.

presidential_document_type.description: Only with type:"presidential_document" — narrows to one sub-type: "executive_order", "proclamation", "memorandum", "determination", "notice", or "other". This is the STRUCTURED way to count/list executive orders etc.; prefer it over a free-text query for "how many X" questions.

executive_order_number.description: Look up ONE executive order by its number, e.g. "14435" or "EO 14435" — automatically scopes to type:"presidential_document" + presidential_document_type:"executive_order" and filters the result to an exact number match, so neither needs to be passed separately. Conflicts with an explicit type/presidential_document_type that names something other than presidential documents / executive orders.

since.description: Publication date floor. Accepts ISO date ("2025-01-01") or shorthand ("30d", "12m", "365d", "1y"). Recommended for any topical search to avoid stale results — the relevance ranker can surface 2004-2008 documents for queries with sparse hits.

tools.name: get_document
tools.description: Get full details for a Federal Register document by its document number (e.g., "2024-12345"). Returns title, abstract, full text link, agencies, dates, and docket information. For a presidential document (executive order, proclamation, memorandum) this also includes executive_order_number, signing_date, and citation.

tools.name: recent_rules
tools.description: Browse the most recently published final rules and regulations from the Federal Register, **with no topic filter** — returns whatever was published most recently across every agency (FAA airworthiness directives, Coast Guard safety zones, EPA tolerance exemptions, etc.). For questions about a specific topic ("EV tax credits", "AI rules", "drug pricing"), use search_documents instead. Returns title, abstract, agency, effective dates, significance.

limit.description: Number of results to return (default 20, max 100)

instructions: @pipeworx/mcp-federal-register forwards to the Pipeworx gateway and lists only the federal-register pack's tools. Set PIPEWORX_META_TOOLS=1 to also list ask_pipeworx and the other gateway-wide tools.
